title: Analytics reconciliation batch coordinator for backfills and schema-migration replays
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We need a robust, auditable way to run large-scale backfills and schema-migration replays for console usage analytics without impacting live traffic or creating duplicate counts in downstream dashboards. Existing ad-hoc replayers are fragile for multi-tenant workloads and lack an easy way to verify data correctness against source-of-truth.

Goal: Build a batch-oriented reconciliation coordinator (Reconciliation Batch Coordinator, RBC) that can: 1) create idempotent replay jobs from the raw event lake (S3) or event broker snapshots, 2) safely shard by tenant/time window and orchestrate parallel workers, 3) enforce rate limits and back-pressure to avoid overloading downstream systems, 4) emit verification artifacts (checksums, sample diffs, reconciliation reports) and 5) integrate with Console dashboards for live progress and health.

Design highlights and decisions so far:
- Orchestration: use Temporal for durable job state and retries (chosen for visibility & easier long-running workflows). Temporal will coordinate Ray worker groups that run Spark jobs for heavy reprocessing tasks. We evaluated pure Flink/Flink-based job reuse but rejected it because our reprocessing jobs are batch-heavy, often require custom Python transforms, and Temporal + Ray offers an easier iteration path for engineers.
- Idempotency: every replayed event will be tagged with a deterministic replay_id + source_checkpoint (S3 prefix + sequence window). Downstream transforms will check for replay_id before materializing results to metrics tables; this requires a small schema change in the metrics ingest (tracked separately).
- Checkpointing: coordinator persists window-level checkpoints and per-shard offsets in Temporal; workers write progress to S3 checkpoint manifests to allow safe retry/resume.
- Verification: each job produces a reconciliation report (counts by metric, hash of input batch, sample rows) and a boolean pass/fail against golden queries run against the current analytics materialized views. Reports are stored under s3://redwood-backfills/reports/{job_id}.
- Throttling & safety: RBC enforces cluster-aware QPS limits per destination (metrics-store, alerts pipeline). We will implement a simulation mode that runs a dry-run of transforms and produces estimated token/row / cost impact before committing writes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Coordinator can spin up and run a 14-day tenant-scoped backfill (10M events) end-to-end on staging without errors and produce reconciliation report.
- No duplicate increments for idempotent runs (run same window twice -> metrics unchanged).
- Console shows job state (queued/running/paused/failed/done) and percent progress + per-shard throughput.
- Rollback path: ability to pause and stop a job and revert writes produced in the last checkpoint window.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for idempotency guard and checkpoint manifest schema.
- Integration: staging backfill with synthetic events (link below) and golden queries.
- Chaos: simulate worker failures and network partitions to validate Temporal retries and manifest resume.

Rollout strategy:
1) Deploy RBC in staging and run two non-customer-impacting backfills (internal tenants).
2) Enable dry-run for first customer backfill and provide PM/Analytics sign-off.
3) Run one small customer backfill under close SRE on-call with runbook.

Operational runbook summary:
- Where to inspect: Temporal UI, RBC dashboard (Console), S3 reports.
- Common failures: missing schemas (preflight checks will detect), rate-limited writes (auto-retry with exponential backoff), worker OOM (increase Ray worker resources).
- Pager: trigger on >30% of shards failing for >10m or reconciliation report mismatch flagged by automated anomaly checks.

Open questions / trade-offs to resolve:
- Should the coordinator offer a simplified \"one-click\" web UI for common backfills, or remain an API-only system for now? (PM leaning toward API-first; UX can be added later).
- Do we require a separate ingest-level idempotency token or rely on metrics-store upserts? Metrics team prefers upserts; small migration required.
- Cost: spinning large Ray+Spark clusters will be expensive. We will prototype a small-emulation mode to estimate cost before running large jobs.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Analytics+Reconciliation+Batch+Coordinator
- Dry-run dataset (staging): s3://redwood-testing/backfill-synthetic/2025-03-01
- GitHub prototype (worker + Temporal wf): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4982
- Dashboard (staging): https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/reconciliation-backfill
- Incident notes from Nov backfill that motivated this: https://docs.redwood.ai/incidents/2024-11-backfill-incident

Next immediate tasks (this ticket):
- Implement Temporal workflow skeleton + state model (Liam)
- Create checkpoint manifest format and S3 writer (Maya)
- Add idempotency header support to metrics ingestion API (depends on metrics infra)
- Build Console staging dashboard widget to display job state and per-shard stats (UX engineer assigned in separate ticket)

Estimated risks: potential increased load on the metrics-store and discovery of old schema variants during replays. We will gate wide replays with a "schema-compatibility" check and require PM signoff for risky tenant backfills.
